branch_hypotheses.alternate_path: A high-signaling enforcement path where precedent setting outweighs delay from negotiation.
branch_hypotheses.divergence_signal: Official announcements specify monetary DMA fines for both Gatekeeper A and Gatekeeper M by the deadline.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Commission concludes both cases with monetary sanctions before 2025-04-30.

branch_hypotheses.alternate_path: Asymmetric enforcement yields a mixed outcome that fails the conjunctive endpoint.
branch_hypotheses.divergence_signal: A monetary fine is announced for one gatekeeper while the other receives no fine, a delayed decision, or only a finding/remedy.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: One case matures faster legally or factually than the other.

branch_hypotheses.alternate_path: Institutional signaling occurs through findings or concessions rather than twin fines.

branch_hypotheses.divergence_signal: No official confirmation of fines for both companies by 2025-04-30 despite continued case activity.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Procedural caution, negotiation, or legal complexity slows one or both cases past the deadline.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Any scenario with only one fine, no fine, or post-deadline action contradicts realization.
endpoint_ledger.description: Monetary DMA fines are officially imposed on both Gatekeeper A and Gatekeeper M by 2025-04-30.
endpoint_ledger.label: Both companies fined by deadline

meta.important_question: Will both Gatekeeper A and Gatekeeper M receive monetary DMA fines by 2025-04-30?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: This is the primary conjunctive benchmark and requires simultaneous success across two separate enforcement tracks.
realization_criteria: official Commission-confirmed monetary fine for Gatekeeper A
official Commission-confirmed monetary fine for Gatekeeper M
both confirmations occur on or before 2025-04-30
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Investigations are active, but no T0 evidence confirms fines yet.

blockers: full delay or non-monetary treatment in both cases
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: If both firms are fined by the deadline, this endpoint fails.

endpoint_ledger.label: Only one company fined by deadline

meta.important_question: Will the Commission impose a monetary fine on only one of the two gatekeepers by 2025-04-30?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: A conjunctive benchmark often fails through uneven case timing or divergent remedy choices.
realization_criteria: official Commission-confirmed monetary fine for exactly one of Gatekeeper A or Gatekeeper M
the other gatekeeper lacks an official monetary fine by 2025-04-30

blockers: Commission chooses monetary sanctions for both cases
no visible action occurs by the deadline

meta.important_question: Will at least one case produce a finding, remedy, or compliance adjustment without a monetary fine by 2025-04-30?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Negotiated compliance changes and interpretive contestation create a credible softer-resolution pathway.
realization_criteria: official action concerning at least one gatekeeper before or by 2025-04-30
the action includes a finding, remedy, commitment, or compliance change
no monetary fine accompanies that action for that gatekeeper by the deadline
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Source text explicitly notes that findings without monetary fines are possible and insufficient for yes.

blockers: Commission finalizes and announces monetary fines for both firms before the deadline
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: This endpoint is contradicted only by timely official fines for both firms.
endpoint_ledger.description: By 2025-04-30, the benchmark condition of monetary fines for both gatekeepers has not been satisfied.
endpoint_ledger.label: Deadline passes without both fines

meta.important_question: Will one or both cases remain unresolved for monetary-fine purposes at the deadline?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: It captures the broad negative space around the conjunctive yes benchmark, including asymmetry, delay, and non-monetary resolutions.
realization_criteria: as of 2025-04-30, fewer than two official Commission-confirmed monetary fines exist across the two cases
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: At initialization the benchmark remains unresolved and multiple pathways fail the conjunctive condition.

merge_hypotheses.mechanism: Both aggressive and cautious observers may converge on accepting delayed or uneven outcomes if legal robustness is emphasized.
If firms offer visible compliance changes, some regulator-firm conflict may converge into a process-focused stalemate rather than immediate sanction escalation.
As the deadline nears, different observer groups converge on the same narrow evidentiary question of whether both fines actually occurred.

simulation_brief.decision_context: European Commission DMA enforcement decisions with separate company-specific findings that jointly determine the benchmark endpoint.
simulation_brief.summary: A new EU digital regulation is being enforced against two large fictionalized gatekeepers. Gatekeeper_A faces scrutiny over app-developer steering restrictions; Gatekeeper_M faces scrutiny over user choice in personal-data use. The key terminal question is whether both receive monetary fines under the Digital Markets Act by 2025-04-30. Early enforcement has signaling value, while both firms have incentives to contest and negotiate. At T0, the process is active but unresolved, with multiple credible paths including fines for both, fines for one, non-monetary findings, delay, or negotiated compliance changes.
uncertainty_notes: No procedural stage beyond active investigation is specified.
No explicit evidence is provided about draft decisions, statement of objections timing, or political appetite for maximal sanctions.
Entity masking limits direct attribution to real firms; actors are fictionalized accordingly.

sociology_baseline.note: Interpretations will shift mostly in response to credible procedural signals, not broad rhetoric.
Visible draft actions, fines, or announced concessions could trigger sharper expression.
Most users remain quiet absent a salient public enforcement moment.
Observers cluster by legal-procedural versus enforcement-signaling priors.
Multiple confirming signals are likely needed before a consensus forms on both-fines likelihood.
Affected groups interpret events through role-based interests.
Attention drifts quickly without concrete Commission announcements.

sociology_prompt_influences.description: Because the DMA is new, early enforcement decisions are interpreted as precedent-setting signals.
Both gatekeepers have incentives to contest legal interpretations and negotiate compliance changes.
The tracked endpoint requires both companies to receive monetary fines by 2025-04-30; non-monetary findings do not satisfy the endpoint.
A single-company fine is insufficient for the benchmark yes outcome, creating a conjunctive endpoint.
